author: high
claim: Direct Bézout plan, existence subgoal: solved.
evidence: Let M_i be the product of the m_j with j≠i (empty product 1). From pairwise coprimality and the identity gcd(r,s)=gcd(r,t)=1 => gcd(r,st)=1, one obtains gcd(M_i,m_i)=1. Choose integers u_i,v_i satisfying u_iM_i+v_im_i=1. Define x=sum_{i=1}^k a_i u_i M_i. For fixed i, u_iM_i≡1 mod m_i, while every M_j with j≠i contains m_i as a factor, so x≡a_i mod m_i. author: high
claim: Direct Bézout plan, uniqueness modulo M subgoal: solved.
evidence: If x and y both solve the congruences, every m_i divides z=x-y. To prove M|z without circularity, first note: if gcd(r,s)=1, r|z, and s|z, write z=rq and choose A,B with Ar+Bs=1. Then q=Az+Bsq, so s|q and rs|z. Induct over the moduli; the partial product m_1...m_h is coprime to m_{h+1}, by iterating gcd(r,s)=gcd(r,t)=1 => gcd(r,st)=1. Hence m_1...m_k divides z, i.e. x≡y mod M.
